text:
HeyGen vient de passer devant ElevenLabs sur le classement des IA de clonage vocal d'Artificial Analysis.

Et leur nouveau modèle a une fonctionnalité que je trouve vraiment sympa.

Tu lui donnes un enregistrement de ta voix, ton texte et la scène de ta vidéo. L'IA reproduit ta façon de parler, ton rythme, tes intonations, mais adapte aussi le son à l'endroit où tu es censé te trouver.

Par exemple, si ta vidéo se déroule dans une usine, ta voix s'adapte au bruit des machines. Si tu es sur une plage, elle prend en compte l'environnement extérieur.

Et il suffit d'un enregistrement de 60 secondes pour commencer à cloner ta voix.

Pour ceux qui font des vidéos avec des voix off générées par IA, ça peut être franchement pratique.

En plus, le modèle est directement intégré à HeyGen, sans supplément.

text:
【響きまで】HeyGenの音声AI、大聖堂でも工場でも「自分の声のまま」。場面に合わせて声を変える仕組みを解説🎙
AI動画のHeyGenが、先日ランキング首位でお伝えした音声モデル「HeyGen Voice」の研究内容を公開しました。ポイントは、声を真似るだけでなく、映像の場面に合わせて「話し方」と「響き」まで整えることです。

仕組みのあらまし
自分の声の録音と原稿、場面の画像を渡すと、AIが画像から「話し方の指示」と「周りの音の指示」を文章で書き起こし、それを手がかりに音声を作ります。マイクの癖や部屋の響きは、声そのものと切り分けて学習させています。そのため、普段の録音から、スタジオ、屋外、大きな会場といった場面向けの音が作れます。長い原稿でも、同じ声と同じ空間が続くようにしています。

聴き比べの結果
🎧 同じ声を50の場面に置き、音と映像が合っているかを伏せて評価。HeyGenが選ばれた割合は、音声AIのCartesiaに対して73%、ElevenLabsに対して70%
🗣 利用者が自分の声の候補を3つ聴いて1つ選ぶ試験（6,153票）では、HeyGenが41.7%で最多。Cartesiaは35.3%、ElevenLabsは23.0%
📚 授業のナレーションに選びたい声を比べる試験では、ElevenLabsに対して61.5%、Cartesiaに対して77.9%

自分のアバター動画を見た43人の評価でも、100点満点で76点と、Cartesiaの63点、ElevenLabsの59点を上回りました。ただし、これらはすべてHeyGenが自社で行った評価です。

安全面
声を複製できるのは、本人の同意が確認できた場合だけです。本人の求めで声を削除でき、生成した音声には、AIが作ったと見分けるための透かしが入ります。

動画の吹き替えやナレーションは、声の質より「その場にいる感じ」が仕上がりを左右することが多いです。声と映像の両方を持つ会社ならではの攻め方に見えます。

text:
At HeyGen, we make one promise to our customers: your video will look like you, sound like you, and move like you.

"Sound like you" is the hard part.

First, the voice has to be yours. That's why we built our own voice model, and it's now ranked #1 in the arena.
But being similar is not enough. Almost every voice model today is trained on podcast data: a studio, a professional mic, a quiet room. That's great for voice agents, phone calls and voiceovers.

Video is a different problem. You might be outside. You might be in a busy office. A car might drive by behind you. And you speak differently to a camera than you do on the phone or a podcast.

So when you put a studio voice into a real scene, it feels off. People can't say why, but they stop believing it.

Some teams try to fix this with multimodal models. So far the quality isn't there, and customers can't get controllability they want. 

We took a different path. We trained our voice model entirely on video data. Years of post-training avatar video models gave us a large proprietary video dataset to learn from. The model reads the scene and adapts both the sound and the delivery to match it.

Today we're launching it: the world’s first video- adaptive voice model, together with state-of-the-art audio quality.

Video that looks real should sound real too.

But being similar is not enough. Almost every voice model today is trained on podcast data: a studio, a professional mic, a quiet room. That's great for voice agents, phone calls and voiceovers.

Video is a different problem. You might be outside. You might be in a busy office. A car might drive by behind you. And you speak differently to a camera than you do on the phone or a podcast.

So when you put a studio voice into a real scene, it feels off. People can't say why, but they stop believing it.

Some teams try to fix this with multimodal models. So far the quality isn't there, and customers can't get controllability they want. 

We took a different path. We trained our voice model entirely on video data. Years of post-training avatar video models gave us a large proprietary video dataset to learn from. The model reads the scene and adapts both the sound and the delivery to match it.

Today we're launching it: the world’s first video- adaptive voice model, together with state-of-the-art audio quality.

Video that looks real should sound real too.

text:
AI voice technology is getting better, but here's the question that really matters: would you trust an AI version of your own voice to represent you?

HeyGen put that question to the test, asking people to watch videos of their digital twins and rate how comfortable they'd feel using those voices themselves.

HeyGen Voice scored 76/100, ahead of Cartesia (63), ElevenLabs v4 (59), and Seedance 2.5 (46).

The goal isn't just to sound human. It's to sound like you.

text:
The first thing I notice with AI voice in video is whether it sounds like it's actually in the room.

A clean studio voice over a factory floor or the front seat of a car never quite matches the shot, and it usually takes work in post to make it fit.

@HeyGen Voice performs your script in your voice and adapts it to the acoustics of the scene. They ran blind tests in 50 locations where reviewers judged whether the sound matched the picture, and they've published the research behind it.

It's built for video first, and it's live in HeyGen today.

text:
This one made me laugh a little.

HeyGen just dropped a new voice model, and the reason they gave for building it is the exact thing my team was complaining about this morning.

They said the avatar voices were giving it away. Like, the face looks real, and then it opens its mouth and you can tell it's AI.

We run an Instagram channel for @tenex_labs where we put out a new AI video several times a week. We use @HeyGen avatars for a lot of those because there’s no way we keep that pace otherwise.

https://t.co/zIhYcrUS1d

But the audio started bugging us enough that we just started recording it ourselves. And while It sounded way better, it also slowed everything down a lot, which kind of defeats the point of using an avatar in the first place.

And then today they drop this. 

They're calling it scene-aware voice cloning. You give it a regular recording of your voice, your script, and a picture of where the avatar is. Then it makes the voice sound like it actually belongs in that spot. So if your avatar is in a podcast studio, it sounds close and warm. If it’s outside, it sounds like it’s outside. 

I haven’t tried it yet, but the examples that they share in the video below are really awesome. i’m excited to throw it at our next batch of videos and see how it does!
